definition: An economic model where human attention is treated as a scarce commodity to be captured, measured, and monetized by digital platforms and advertisers.
metaDescription: Learn about the attention economy - how digital platforms monetize your focus and attention as a valuable resource in the modern internet age.
simpleExplanation: The attention economy is the idea that your focus and attention have become valuable resources that companies compete to capture. Social media platforms, websites, and apps are designed to grab and hold your attention for as long as possible to show you ads.
whyItMatters: Understanding the attention economy helps explain why social media can feel addictive and why your personal data is so valuable. It reveals how 'free' platforms actually make money and why they use persuasive design to keep you engaged.
technicalDetail: The attention economy operates through engagement metrics like time-on-site, click-through rates, and user interactions. Platforms use algorithmic feeds, push notifications, and behavioral psychology techniques to maximize attention capture, then sell this aggregated attention to advertisers through targeted advertising systems.

examples.explanation: Facebook and Instagram use endless scrolling feeds designed to keep you browsing indefinitely, maximizing the time you spend viewing ads between posts.
YouTube automatically plays the next video to prevent you from leaving the platform, keeping your attention engaged so they can show more advertisements.
Apps send frequent push notifications to recapture your attention throughout the day, bringing you back to view more content and ads.
